e-13020.problem: Use the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^6$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(1.15)^6.$ Give your answer to three decimal places.
e-13020.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{1}{2!} n(n-1)x^2 + \dfrac{1}{3!} n(n-1)(n-2)x^3 + \cdots + x^n.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{6} & =1+6x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot {x}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot {x}^{3}+⋯+{x}^{n} \\  & =1+6x+15{x}^{2}+20{x}^{3}+⋯\,+{x}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
\left( {1 + x} \right)^6 \approx 1 + 6x + 15x^2 + 20x^3.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=0.15$ into the above approximation of $(1 + x)^6{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.15)^{6} & =(1+0.15)^{6} \\  & ≈1+6(0.15)^{1}+15(0.15)^{2}+20(0.15)^{3} \\  & =1+6(0.15)+15(0.022\,5)+20(0.003\,375) \\  & =1+0.9+0.337\,5+0.067\,5 \\  & =2.305,\end{aligned}
$$

to three decimal places.

e-13021.problem: Use the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^8$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(0.89)^8.$ Give your answer to six decimal places.
e-13021.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{1}{2!} n(n-1)x^2 + \dfrac{1}{3!} n(n-1)(n-2)x^3 + \cdots + x^n.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{8} & =1+8x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot {x}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot {x}^{3}+⋯+{x}^{n} \\  & =1+8x+28{x}^{2}+56{x}^{3}+⋯\,+{x}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
\left( {1 + x} \right)^8 \approx 1 + 8x + 28x^2 + 56x^3.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-0.11$ into the above approximation of $(1 + x)^8{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0.89)^{8} & =(1+(-0.11))^{8} \\  & ≈1+8(-0.11)^{1}+28(-0.11)^{2}+56(-0.11)^{3} \\  & =1-8(0.11)+28(0.012\,1)-56(0.001\,331) \\  & =1-0.88+0.338\,8-0.074\,536 \\  & =0.384\,264,\end{aligned}
$$

to six decimal places.

e-13023.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.08)^{5}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^5$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
e-13023.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem for positive integer $n$ states that

$$
{(a + b)^n} = {n \choose 0}{a^n}{b^0} + {n \choose 1}{a^{n - 1}}{b^1} + {n \choose 2}{a^{n - 2}}{b^2} +  \ldots  + {n \choose n}{a^0}{b^n}.
$$

By substituting $a = 1,$ $b = x,$ and $n = 5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(1)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(1)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(1)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(1)}^{5}+5{(1)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(1)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+5(1)(x)+10(1)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =1+5x+10{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{\left( {1 + x} \right)^{5}} \approx 1 + 5x + 10x^2.
$$

Now, we substitute $x = 0.08$ into the above approximation of $(1 + x)^5{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.08)^{5} & =(1+0.08)^{5} \\  & ≈1+5(0.08)+10(0.08)^{2} \\  & =1+5(0.08)+10(0.006\,4) \\  & =1+0.4+0.064 \\  & =1.464\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.08)^{5}-1.464|}{(1.08)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.36%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

content.problem: Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{5}$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(0.94)^{5}.$ Give your answer to three decimal places.
content.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{5} & =1+5x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{5} \\  & =1+5x+10{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{5}≈1+5x+10{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-0.06$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{5}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0.94)^{6} & =(1+(-0.06))^{5} \\  & ≈1+5(-0.06)+10(-0.06)^{2} \\  & =1-5(0.06)+10(0.003\,6) \\  & =1-0.3+0.036 \\  & =0.736,\end{aligned}
$$

to three decimal places.

(1+x)7≈1+7x+21x2+35x3.

Question 13
?

Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (4+x)4 in ascending powers of x to approximate (4.05)4. Give your answer to three decimal places.

a
269.044
b
269.046
c
269.042
d
269.038
e
269.040
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The binomial theorem for positive integer n states that

(a+b)n=(n0)anb0+(n1)an−1b1+(n2)an−2b2+…+(nn)a0bn.

By substituting a=4, b=x, and n=4, we obtain

(4+x)4=(40)(4)4(x)0+(41)(4)4−1(x)1+(42)(4)4−2(x)2+⋯=1(4)4+4(4)3(x)1+6(4)2(x)2+⋯=256+4(64)(x)+6(16)(x2)+⋯=256+256x+96x2+⋯.

So, for small x, we have

(4+x)4≈256+256x+96x2+⋯.

Finally, we substitute x=0.05 into the expansion of (4+x)4:

(4.05)4=(4+0.05)4≈256+256(0.05)+96(0.05)2=256+256(0.05)+96(0.0025)=256+12.8+0.24=269.040,

to three decimal places.

after.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.02)^{7}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{7}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{7} & =1+7x+\frac{1}{2!}\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n} \\  & =1+7x+21{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{7}≈1+7x+21{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=0.02$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{7}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.02)^{7} & =(1+0.02)^{7} \\  & ≈1+7(0.02)+21(0.02)^{2} \\  & =1+7(0.02)+21(0.000\,4) \\  & =1+0.14+0.008\,4 \\  & =1.148\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.02)^{7}-1.148\,4|}{(1.02)^{7}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.02%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

after.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.98)^{5}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(2+x)^{5}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to one decimal place.
after.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem for positive integer $n$ states that

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

By substituting $a=2,$ $b=x,$ and $n=5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(2+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(2)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(2)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(2)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(2)}^{5}+5{(2)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(2)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1(32)+5(16)(x)+10(8)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =32+80x+80{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(2+x)}^{5}≈32+80x+80{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=-0.02$ into the above approximation of $(2+x)^{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.98)^{5} & =(2+(-0.02))^{5} \\  & ≈32+80(-0.02)+80(-0.02)^{2} \\  & =32-80(0.02)+80(0.000\,4) \\  & =32-1.6+0.032 \\  & =30.432\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.98)^{5}-30.432|}{(1.98)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.0%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.

after.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(2.1)^{5}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(2+x)^{5}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem for positive integer $n$ states that

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

By substituting $a=2,$ $b=x,$ and $n=5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(2+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(2)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(2)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(2)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(2)}^{5}+5{(2)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(2)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1(32)+5(16)(x)+10(8)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =32+80x+80{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(2+x)}^{5}≈32+80x+80{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=0.1$ into the above approximation of $(2+x)^{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(2.1)^{5} & =(2+0.1)^{5} \\  & ≈32+80(0.1)+80(0.1)^{2} \\  & =32+80(0.1)+80(0.01) \\  & =32+8+0.8 \\  & =40.8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(2.1)^{5}-40.8|}{(2.1)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.10%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

The binomial theorem for positive integer $n$ states that

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

By substituting $a=2,$ $b=x,$ and $n=5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(2+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(2)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(2)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(2)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(2)}^{5}+5{(2)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(2)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1(32)+5(16)(x)+10(8)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =32+80x+80{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(2+x)}^{5}≈32+80x+80{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=0.1$ into the above approximation of $(2+x)^{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(2.1)^{5} & =(2+0.1)^{5} \\  & ≈32+80(0.1)+80(0.1)^{2} \\  & =32+80(0.1)+80(0.01) \\  & =32+8+0.8 \\  & =40.8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(2.1)^{5}-40.8|}{(2.1)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.10%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
